children: Yields on U.K. government bonds, or gilts, climb as investors await the reopening of the January 2056 gilt via syndication on Tuesday. Traders could demand a higher risk premium to buy the gilt, given U.K. inflation concerns due to high energy prices, and fiscal pressures, Mizuho's Evelyne Gomez-Liechti says in a note. The outcome of the gilt syndication is likely to set the tone for the gilt yield curve, Gomez-Liechti says. "A strong book would help stabilize the 30-year gilt sector," she says, "But we would not read too much into demand unless the bond performs after pricing." U.K. 30-year gilt yields rise 1.1 basis points to last trade at 5.826%, Tradeweb data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
